svg.title: How snodo runs a task
svg.desc: Three runs loop. First, a clean pass: an agent dispatches a task over MCP, pre-execute validators issue a signed token, a coder writes the change in its own worktree, post-execute validators run the tests, and the work arrives as a pull request. Second, a warning: the findings go back to the coder, which corrects the change and tries again until the validators pass. Third, a single blocker halts the run before anything is written. Every step is appended to a hash-chained audit log.
svg.text: snodo enforces your process around whichever agent writes the code

g.text: ● human revises the intent → run again

svg.text: modes tool sets · validators must agree · policy warn retries, a blocker goes to a human

g.text: findings fed back · retry* until pass
re-written intent goes back to the start

svg.text: The coder is interchangeable and separate from the judge. A warning goes back to the coder, which corrects and retries up to the
recovery depth. A blocker cannot be outvoted: a human acknowledges it and revises the intent. Every decision is appended to the audit log.
